issues.t: Cruise control switch can start an engine fire (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning plastic smell from under the hood near the brake master cylinder, often while the truck is parked and turned off. Owners have reported trucks burning in driveways and garages.
issues.why: The cruise control (speed control) deactivation switch sits on the brake master cylinder. Brake fluid can seep into its electrical side, and because the switch has power even with the key off, it can overheat and catch fire. Ford recalled these trucks to disconnect the switch and later to add a fused wiring harness.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 05V-388 now. Until it is done, park outside and away from buildings. If you see smoke from the hood, get away from the truck and call the fire department.

issues.t: Tailgate rear window can shatter on its own
issues.sym: A loud bang and the tailgate glass breaks into the cargo area, often soon after the rear defroster is turned on, and sometimes while parked. Some owners had it happen more than once.
issues.why: Owners and dealers linked it to stress in the glass around the defroster grid and the window seal; one owner cited a Ford bulletin blaming a reaction between the weatherstrip and the defroster element. Replacing only the glass may not stop it from happening again.
issues.next: Have a glass shop or Ford dealer replace the glass and the seal together. Until then, avoid running the rear defroster for long periods and keep passengers out of the cargo area.

issues.t: Anti-lock brakes fail or pull to one side
issues.sym: ABS warning light, the truck pulling to one side when braking, wheels locking up, or a brake pedal that does not seem to slow the truck.
issues.why: Owners filed several federal complaints about the four-wheel anti-lock brake system on 1996 Broncos. On a truck this old, causes include a failed wheel speed sensor, a sticking brake caliper, a leaking brake line or a faulty ABS hydraulic unit.
issues.next: Do not ignore a brake warning light or a pull. Have the brake system and ABS codes checked before driving any distance.

issues.t: E4OD automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Slipping under hard acceleration, surging at stops, delayed or missing shifts, or the truck refusing to move forward.
issues.why: The heavy-duty E4OD four-speed automatic used in these Broncos is a common failure point, and owners reported failures to federal regulators. Old fluid and heat speed up wear.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and smell. If it is dark or burnt, or the transmission slips, have a transmission shop diagnose it before it fails completely.

issues.t: Intake valve can break and destroy the engine (recall)
issues.sym: A sudden loud ticking or knocking, misfires, a check-engine light, loss of power, or the engine quitting while driving.
issues.why: On some 2.7L and 3.0L twin-turbo V6 engines, an intake valve can break and drop into the cylinder, which ruins the engine and causes a loss of drive power.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-635. The dealer runs an engine test and replaces the engine if it fails. If you hear a sudden knock, pull over and shut the engine off.

issues.t: Internal engine failure can cause loss of power (recalls)
issues.sym: Knocking, misfires, warning lights, loss of power, or the engine shutting off.
issues.why: Some newer engines may fail internally; recall 26V-343 covers 2025-2026 trucks and recall 26V-548 covers 2026 trucks with pistons that may have been made with the wrong dome shape.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 26V-343 and 26V-548. If the engine starts knocking, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Engine bay wiring can rub through and short (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning plastic smell from under the hood, warning lights, or electrical items cutting out.
issues.why: A wiring harness in the engine compartment can chafe against nearby parts until the insulation wears through and shorts, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-468. If you smell burning wires, park outside away from buildings and call the dealer.

issues.t: Hardtop roof panel can separate (recall)
issues.sym: Creaking, flexing, cracks or gaps in the molded-in-color hardtop, wind noise, or water getting in.
issues.why: Molded-in-color hardtop roof panels on some early Broncos can come apart, and a piece could come off while driving.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-299. Do not drive at highway speed with a cracked or loose roof panel.

issues.t: Fender flares can come off (recall)
issues.sym: Fender flares rattle, flap or are missing after a drive.
issues.why: Some fender flares may not have been secured properly and can detach, becoming a road hazard.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-403. Push on each flare; if it moves, get it fixed.

issues.t: Front seat height bolt can loosen (recalls)
issues.sym: The front seat feels loose, rocks, clunks, or tilts when you sit or brake.
issues.why: A pivot bolt in the front seat height-adjust mechanism may loosen or fall out, so the seat may not hold you in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 25V-721 (2021-2023) and 26V-268 (2024-2026).

issues.t: Transfer case joint worn after an earlier repair (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks, grinding or vibration from under the middle of the truck, or loss of drive.
issues.why: On trucks that had earlier transmission or transfer case work, the joint between them may have been put back misaligned, wearing out the splines.
issues.next: If your transmission or transfer case has been replaced, check your VIN for recall 26V-236.

issues.t: Backup camera stays on after reversing (recalls)
issues.sym: The backup camera picture stays on the screen after you shift out of reverse, hiding other information.
issues.why: A SYNC infotainment software fault. Ford has had to redo some repairs, so there are several follow-up recalls.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 22V-825, 23V-165, 25V-312 and 25V-888.

issues.t: Backup camera blank, frozen or delayed (recalls)
issues.sym: The backup or 360-degree camera shows nothing, freezes, or comes on late when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: Faulty cameras on some 2021 trucks (23V-598), 360-degree cameras on 2022-2023 trucks (25V-273), and software faults or an overheating radio module on newer trucks (25V-315, 26V-124).
issues.next: Check your VIN for these recalls. Look behind you and use your mirrors until it is fixed.

issues.t: Engine block heater can crack and short out (recall)
issues.sym: Coolant leaking near the block heater or the outlet tripping when it is plugged in.
issues.why: The factory block heater can crack, leak coolant and short-circuit when plugged in, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Do not plug in the block heater until the recall is done. Check your VIN for recall 25V-685.

issues.t: Rear shock reservoir can rust and break off (recall)
issues.sym: A bouncy or harsh ride, oil on the rear shocks, or a shock reservoir hanging loose.
issues.why: Rear shocks with external reservoirs can corrode, and the reservoir can come loose from the shock.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-025. Look at the rear shocks for rust or oil.

issues.t: Low-pressure fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Hesitation, loss of power, or the engine stalling while driving or not starting.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump in the tank may fail. Ford updates the engine computer software on these trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-455. If it stalls, get to a safe spot.

issues.t: Rear door can open with the child lock on (recalls)
issues.sym: A rear door opens from the inside even though the child safety lock is set.
issues.why: The rear door latch or child lock may not work correctly. Several recalls cover different years and doors.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 22V-411, 24V-189, 25V-303 and 25V-397. Until it is fixed, do not count on the child lock.

issues.t: Front control arm or ball joint fasteners may be loose (recalls)
issues.sym: Clunks from the front, loose or wandering steering. A control arm could come apart.
issues.why: Bolts or nuts on the front upper ball joints or lower control arms may be missing or not tightened. Some of these are do-not-drive recalls.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 24V-770, 25V-260, 25V-308 and 25V-310. If yours is a do-not-drive recall, have it towed.

issues.t: Transmission may not engage Reverse or may creep (recall)
issues.sym: The truck does not go into reverse, or moves when you do not expect it.
issues.why: The transmission valve body may have been machined incorrectly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-164. Always set the parking brake until it is fixed.

issues.t: Truck may not hold in Park (recalls)
issues.sym: The truck may roll after it is put in Park.
issues.why: A loose bolt (23V-070) or a park pawl damaged during assembly (23V-546) can stop Park from engaging.
issues.next: Always use the parking brake. Check your VIN for both recalls.

issues.t: Steering gear can bind or get hard to turn (recall)
issues.sym: Steering that suddenly feels heavy, binds, or will not turn.
issues.why: Internal damage in the steering gear can increase steering effort or even lock the wheel. Ford told owners not to drive until it is fixed.
issues.next: Do not drive the truck if it is under recall 23V-155. Have it towed to a dealer.

issues.t: Driver-side lug nuts may be loose (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: A clicking or clunking from a wheel, or a vibration that gets worse.
issues.why: Lug nuts on the driver-side wheels of some 2023 trucks were not tightened properly.
issues.next: Do not drive it until checked. Check your VIN for recall 23V-283.

issues.t: Rear quarter window can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise, rattling or a gap around a rear side window.
issues.why: Rear quarter glass may not have been installed correctly and could detach.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-142.

issues.t: Windshield may not be fully bonded (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise or water leaks around the windshield.
issues.why: The windshield may not have been glued in properly and could come out in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 22V-451.

issues.t: Windshield bonding can fail on 2025 models (recall)
issues.sym: Wind noise or water leaks around the windshield.
issues.why: The windshield on some 2025 trucks may not be bonded properly and could come out in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-683.

issues.t: Electronic brake booster can lose power assist (recalls)
issues.sym: A brake warning light and a hard brake pedal that needs much more force to stop.
issues.why: The electronic brake booster can malfunction. Some trucks get a software update (25V-488) and others a new booster (25V-823).
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls. Leave extra stopping distance until it is fixed.

issues.t: Instrument cluster can go dark at startup (recall)
issues.sym: The gauges and warning lights do not come on when you start the truck.
issues.why: A software fault in the instrument cluster.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-788. Do not drive if you cannot see your speed.

issues.t: EGR valve can fail and cut engine power (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, reduced-power mode and a check-engine light.
issues.why: The exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) valve may fail.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-122.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump bolts can loosen and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell from the engine bay or a check-engine light.
issues.why: The mounting bolts on the high-pressure fuel pump may not have been tightened enough, letting fuel leak.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, park outside and call the dealer. Check your VIN for recall 25V-597.

issues.t: Side impact sensors may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: Side impact sensors may not be fastened properly, so side airbags might not deploy correctly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 22V-928.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not deploy correctly (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms before a crash.
issues.why: A vent on the passenger front airbag may open too early, so it does not protect as designed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-770.

issues.t: Passenger airbag vent flap may block deployment (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms before a crash.
issues.why: A vent flap inside the passenger airbag may keep it from inflating as designed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-396.

issues.t: Right side curtain airbag can tear on deployment (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms before a crash.
issues.why: A burr on a mounting bracket can cut the right side curtain airbag as it inflates.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-580.

issues.t: Front seat belts hard to reach (recall)
issues.sym: The front seat belt latch slides down and is hard to grab, especially with the doors off.
issues.why: The latch plate can drop out of easy reach when the belt is stowed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-358; the dealer adds a stop button to the belt.

issues.t: Front radar may be misaligned (recall)
issues.sym: Adaptive cruise control or automatic emergency braking acts up, or a sensor warning appears.
issues.why: The front radar sensor may be aimed at the wrong angle.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-982.
